## LLM Recipe

### 1.1 Data Curation &amp; Tokenization

#### [General progress substitutes for specific training data in language models](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24844>)

Controlled training experiments withhold skill-specific supervision and later restore it to measure how general model progress changes the additional data needed to acquire a skill. Across synthetic domains and web-text models up to 7B, more advanced checkpoints often learn the withheld skills with fewer additional tokens, motivating adaptation tests alongside capability scores when evaluating data-filtering strategies. Target masking preserves the original inputs, and the whole-domain Rust experiment retains residual data, so the results do not establish that filtering is ineffective in general.

### 1.3 Pretraining &amp; Optimization

#### [Do Frontier Model Ingredients Add Up? A Replicated Factorial Study of Small Language Models](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24540>)

A replicated factorial experiment tests five modern training ingredients jointly in small language models, separating average recipe effects from interactions and run noise. The 32-run study finds mostly additive loss gains within its tested settings, while showing why shared baselines, replication and explicit aliasing assumptions are needed before transferring isolated improvements into a combined recipe.

### 1.8 Distillation &amp; Model Compression

#### [On-Policy Morphing into Hybrid Attention Models](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24809>)

FlashMorph2 selects which Transformer layers retain full attention by sampling discrete hybrid architectures, propagating their own hidden states and adapting shared weights during the selection stage. Under matched subsequent recovery, it improves average long-context and recall scores over FlashMorph across the tested Qwen configurations, providing a practical way to account for interactions that frozen, continuously mixed layer scoring misses.

#### [GRAFT: Execution-Guided Genetic Recombination for Agent Design](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23509>)

GRAFT gives an evolutionary agent-program designer bounded examples of each parent’s successes and failures, alongside its code and aggregate fitness. Controlled searches improve held-out performance when this evidence is added, offering a way to turn evaluation logs into architectural changes without extra task executions to collect that feedback. Some gains reflect interface normalization, and the study does not establish long-horizon transfer or equal total inference cost.

ARISE turns failed enterprise-agent runs into retrievable corrections and a compact set of rules, checking rule updates on held-out training validation while keeping model weights, tools and workflow fixed. ## AI Training &amp; Inference Infra

### 3.3 Inference Engines &amp; Serving

#### [Harvesting Expert-Parallel Bubbles for Fine-Tuning](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24496>)

BubbleTea predicts each GPU’s idle window inside an expert-parallel MoE layer and fills it with compiler-generated LoRA training chunks that share serving weights. On four A100 GPUs with BF16 serving across three MoE models, it delivers 1.9–6.2× the fine-tuning throughput of a ported LLMStation baseline while keeping both p90 TTFT and TPOT within 10% of serving alone in 50 of 63 workloads. It offers a concrete way to reclaim serving capacity, but those gains include improved decode/idle-time execution; residual bubble filling adds 12–23% at high load with expert load balancing, and some configurations substantially worsen serving latency.

#### [Cap-and-Track: Optimizing LLM Inference Request Dispatch Across Shifting Capacity](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24891>)

Cap-and-Track keeps excess asynchronous inference work in durable priority queues, combines prompt per-replica refusals with a refusal-driven dispatcher, and follows capacity changes without predicting output length. In a same-traffic production A/B, Meta’s complete shaper served a classifier on 39 H100s versus 68 for its fixed-rate precursor with matching coverage and scores; controlled real-engine replay separately tests admission and dispatch. The design is useful for latency-tolerant backfills and media processing, but the smaller fleet trades lower-priority freshness for utilization: the lowest band waited a median 6.6 hours versus 0.5 hours at backfill peaks, and interactive or agent-session traffic was not evaluated.

Track takes220s to95% after restore; fixed pre-drop rate recovers immediately, and moderate40%capacity losses can take~13minutes to descend. Emulator/simulation comparisons are identified separately, not claimed as GPU measurements. Original LG NEW Thu19, v1 receipt Wed18 18:34:10UTC(13:34EST), and Tuesday14–Wednesday14 -&gt; Wednesday20EST schedule support Nov19 01Z public availability. Earliest successful team discovery is Recipe LG NEW completed11:07:13.983332UTC; copied rawcatalog/receipt pinned. No earlier matching public full study located in bounded primary/native/web search. No author code or reproducible raw production logs verified; unrelated GitHub name matches excluded.

**Limitations:** Only asynchronous, latency-tolerant work with prompt labeled refusals and one controller/capacity domain; no interactive or agent-session serving validation. Production A/B identifies the whole shaper change, not refusal-only control in isolation; other provider comparisons are observational and confounded by backlog/admission/token-mix changes. Classifier fleet43%reduction is39vs68 in the comparison, not current45production sizing; low-priority freshness worsens, with44–55% meeting goals during backfill. Larger fleet capacity-savings extrapolations, prefix-aware ordering, queue autoscaling and general framework-stack integration are untested. Real-engine controller replay is classifier-shaped with synthetic prompts; generative production results are observational. Slow adaptation/freezes and refusal/network overhead remain. Controller code, traces, raw logs and production model details are not publicly verified; no independent reproduction.

### 3.8 Hardware, Networking &amp; Cluster Efficiency

#### [A Fast, Programmable GPU-to-CPU Invocation Layer for GPU-Initiated Communication](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23848>)

A new KIWI study evaluates programmable CPU-proxy communication built on the existing public invocation library, using per-wave queues and workload-specific host callbacks to simplify MoE dispatch and combine. On MI300X nodes with 400 Gb/s RoCE links, its BF16 expert-parallel benchmark reaches up to 2.3× lower dispatch-plus-combine latency than the best tested backend, while separate FP8 GLM-5.3 vLLM experiments reduce TPOT by up to 29% versus MORI. The results make CPU-assisted networking worth considering for low-latency MoE serving, with four proxy CPU cores per GPU and weaker performance at some larger token counts; they establish a new measured study rather than a new software release.

**Published:** 2026-11-18 · **First seen:** 2026-11-19T11:07:13.983+00:00 · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** GPU Communication, CPU Proxies, Expert Parallelism, AMD Instinct

**Public availability:** 2026-11-19T01:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.DC/new?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.23848v1>) · [Code](<https://github.com/AMDResearch/kiwi>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Read complete scientific main pp.1–9; pp.9–11 references not separately read in full. Actual p.7 TableIII/Figs.5–6 and p.8 Figs.7–8 directly inspected. GPU waves publish descriptor+signal pairs into SPSC host-memory queues through wave-wide stores; ordinary application-owned CPU threads poll endpoints and execute registered callbacks. Data still moves GPU-to-GPU via NIC RDMA; only protocol/control moves to the host. KIWI-EP defines multicast, count all-to-all and barrier callbacks plus dynamic active-range polling and skewed round-robin endpoint ownership. The queue1.92us p50 unloaded RTT and earlier core design are not presented as newly released results. New full paper provides2–8node MI300X measurements:8GPUs/node,8ConnectX-7 400Gb/s RoCE NICs/node,PCIeGen5,NUMA pinning,median at least3runs. BF16 DeepSeekV3-shaped EP uses hidden7168/256experts/top8 and reports slowest-rank dispatch+combine latency: best tested up to16tokens/GPU on2nodes,32on4,all tested on8; maximum2.3x. Separate FP8 GLM5.3 PD-disaggregated vLLM serves8Kinput/1Koutput;NPND denotes N prefill PLUS N decode nodes,8ranks/node. Prefill stays MORI; only decode switches backend. TPOT improves up to29% over MORI; GSM8K/needle checks report no accuracy effect without detailed confidence intervals. Repository history/initial tree and historical README/docs were inspected: initial full library/prototype EP code Nov6, queue/performance README Nov17, paper link Nov19. The initial tree contains implementation, benchmark drivers and tuning tables, but no raw experiment-result artifacts or paper; bounded inspected initial documentation does not disclose the paper’s2.3x/29% comparative study. Thus the report concerns the newly disclosed measured manuscript, not invention/release of previously available callbacks/EP code. Primary DC NEW Thu19 and v1 receipt Wed18 04:52:50UTC (=Tue23:52EST) support Wednesday20EST/Nov19 01Z public announcement by official schedule. First actual completed team discovery is Recipe LG NEW Nov19 11:07:13.983332UTC, copied/pinned. Public repository landing, API and README verified200; source and tests not executed.

**Limitations:** Earlier public library and prototype EP code date Nov6, so no new-method or new-code-release claim. AMD MI300X/RoCE-specific comparative evidence, not all GPUs/networks; host proxy CPU resource/pinning requirements are material. Four CPU proxy cores/GPU in EP deployment; ordinary OS thread preemption is unmodeled. KIWI sends a token once per destination GPU, while MORI can send once per destination node, so at higher token counts on2/4nodes it can lose. NPND serving scale is two fleets and is not the same experiment as the2–8node microbenchmark. Some queue baseline protocols are reimplemented on AMD and callbacks reduce bare-queue throughput. No reported software-version pin for the paper’s full cluster, no raw run records or detailed quality uncertainty inspected, no broad semantic/accuracy guarantee, no independent reproduction.
